title: UK labour market overview — earnings, unemployment and vacancies (ONS, 07:00 London / 02:00 ET), the last labour read before the 2027-02-04 Monetary Policy Report round
source: EST: two UK-government primaries RE-FETCHED direct 2026-09-09 by this event's own lane, both HTTP 200, rather than inherited from the proposal. (1) gov.uk/government/statistics/announcements/uk-labour-market-january-2027 — the statutory pre-announcement register reads 'UK Labour Market: January 2027', '19 January 2027 7:00am (confirmed)', producer Office for National Statistics, designation 'Accredited official statistics'. (2) ons.gov.uk/releases/uklabourmarketjanuary2027 — the ONS release-calendar entry reads 'UK Labour Market: January 2027', release date '19 January 2027 at 7:00am', marked 'Not yet published', contents 'Estimates of employment, unemployment, inactivity, average weekly earnings, vacancies and other labour market related statistics for the UK'. Filed estimate per this lane's no-self-confirm limit and because the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts carries BLS:/BEA:/CENSUS:/FED: and has no slot for the UK Office for National Statistics — the same gap all four 2026 siblings were filed under. The DATE is not in doubt; the estimate label is about the taxonomy, not the evidence
notes: RESEARCHED 2026-09-09 by its own lane (docs/research/events/uk-labour-market-2027-01-19.md), which read the single proposal in full — proposals/uk-labour-market-2027-01-19.from-uk-labour-market-2026-12-15.json, now inert and left in place — and re-fetched every primary rather than inheriting it. THE TITLE IS CHANGED, AND THAT IS THE HEADLINE FINDING. The proposal's title reads 'the first whose AWE window is wholly post-Budget'; its own notes refute that claim in the same file, and this lane's arithmetic refutes it a second way. (1) THE CHAIN'S CORRECTION IS ITSELF OFF BY ONE RELEASE. Both the proposal and the 12-15 ledger's leg 8 state that the first wholly post-Budget AWE window 'publishes in the FEBRUARY 2027 release'. By the window rule those same documents verified — the headline AWE/LFS window is the three months ending TWO months before the release month, reconfirmed firsthand today from the 18 August 2026 bulletin (Apr-Jun AWE/LFS, May-Jul vacancies, Jul payroll flash) — the February 2027 release carries OCT-DEC 2026, and October is 27/31 pre-Budget. The first wholly post-Budget window, NOV 2026-JAN 2027, publishes in the MARCH 2027 release, whose own anchor proves the rule: the March 2026 release carried Nov 2025-Jan 2026. That release is dated 16 March 2027 07:00, 'Confirmed' on the gov.uk register fetched today, and it precedes the 18 March 2027 MPC round at D-2. So the chain has now corrected 'wholly post-Budget' three times and landed the answer in the wrong month twice; this entry's own AWE window is SEP-NOV 2026, of which 33 of 91 days are post-Budget. (2) THE PLACEMENT CLAIM IS SETTLED BY REGISTER, NOT BY PRECEDENT, AND IT IS THE STRONGEST IN THE CHAIN. The 12-15 lane had to argue a D-2 print into a non-Report round from two precedents. This print is D-16 from the 2027-02-04 round, and the NEXT labour print is 2027-02-16 ('16 February 2027 at 7:00am (confirmed)', gov.uk register fetched today) — twelve days AFTER that round. bankofengland.co.uk/monetary-policy/upcoming-mpc-dates, fetched today, lists 4 February 2027 as provisional and as 'February MPC Summary and minutes and February Monetary Policy Report'. So this is unambiguously the last labour read before a FORECAST round, not merely before a vote — no inference required. (3) NO ABSOLUTE WAGE THRESHOLD IS REGISTERED, AND THE REFUSAL IS THE CALL. The Sep-Nov window is ONE month of 2026 Q3 and TWO of Q4 — the inverse of the 12-15 window's 2/3-Q3 mix — so the majority of it sits in the quarter for which the July 2026 MPR publishes no private-AWE path at all (2.8% Q2, ~3.0% Q3, then nothing; independently re-checked today). Setting a level from a path covering one third of the window would be weaker than the sibling's, and the anchor arrives first: the Bank's own page lists 2026-11-05 as CONFIRMED and as a Monetary Policy Report round, 75 days before this print. This lane registers a RELATIVE test instead (Sep-Nov at or above Aug-Oct, which needs no Q4 level) and pre-commits the absolute one to the first pulse after 2026-11-05. (4) FOUR DATED ADJACENCIES PROPOSED, INCLUDING A REAL CALENDAR GAP: this calendar carries boe-decision entries for 2026-12-17, 2027-04-29, 2027-06-17 and 2027-11-04 but NONE for 2027-02-04 or 2027-03-18, both listed on the Bank's own upcoming-dates page today. The 02-04 round is the single thing this print most directly feeds. IMPACT LOW, argued not inherited: symbols [], this repo tracks no UK-listed symbol, no house playbook is rates- or sterling-keyed, and the measured cable reaction to the 2026-08-18 release was ~0.1% on a two-sided beat. THE CORRIDOR IS THE CLEANEST OF THE FIVE UK LABOUR ENTRIES BY COUNT AND THE ODDEST BY SHAPE: 13 tracked events within five days against 35 for the 12-15 sibling, but D-1 is mlk-market-closure-2027-01-18 (US markets shut Monday, UK open), so the print lands in the pre-open of the FIRST US session after a three-day weekend and any US-open attribution is worse than the thin corridor suggests; fomc-blackout-start-2027-01-16 sits at D-3 with fomc-2027-01-27 at D+8, so unlike the 12-15 sibling a Fed blackout IS running; wef-davos-annual-meeting-2027-01-18 puts the print on day 2 of Davos; and uk-cpi-2027-01-20 (proposal only) makes the UK run two days again with this print first. Estimate widens caution only; nothing date-keyed may act on this.
